title: Multiplying Whole Numbers and Fractions
seo_title: Grade 5 Multiplying Whole Numbers and Fractions Worksheets (TEKS 5.3I, STAAR)
standard_text: 5.3I represent and solve for products of a fraction and a whole number using objects and pictorial models, including area models
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 worksheets for Texas TEKS 5.3I: multiply whole numbers and fractions with counters and bar models, repeated addition, comparing products and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply the whole number by the top number; keep the bottom number.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 3 × 25 means 3 groups of 2/5: 2/5 + 2/5 + 2/5 = 6/5.
  • Multiply the whole number by the top number and keep the bottom number.
  • A fraction of a number: 2/3 of 12 means split 12 into 3 equal groups and take 2 of them: 8.
  • Multiplying by a fraction less than 1 gives a product smaller than the whole number.

Examples

Example

4 × 3/8

4 × 3 = 12

12/8

Simplify

Answer: 1 1/2

Example

2/3 of 12

12 ÷ 3 = 4

4 × 2

Answer: 8

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying the bottom number too: 3 × 2/5 = 6/15The bottom number tells the size of the parts. It does not change.
Adding: 3 × 2/5 = 3 2/5Multiply 3 by the top number.
Thinking the product is always bigger2/3 × 12 = 8, which is less than 12.

faq.q: How do you multiply a whole number by a fraction?
faq.a: Multiply the whole number by the numerator and keep the denominator. Then simplify.
Yes. Multiplication can be done in any order. Both equal 15/4 = 3 3/4.
You are taking half of 10, which is 5.

items.q: The 12 counters are in 3 equal groups. What is 23 of 12?
items.e: Split 12 into 3 equal parts: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 in each part. Take 2 of the parts: 2 × 4 = 8. So 23 × 12 = 8. In the picture, 2 of the 3 groups are shaded.

sets.title: Is the product bigger or smaller?

items.q: The top bar is 12. The bottom bar shows 34 × 12. Without multiplying, how does 34 × 12 compare with 12?
items.e: 34 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so 34 × 12 is less than 12. It is only part of 12. You do not need to multiply. In the picture, the bottom bar has 3 equal parts and the top bar has 4.

items.q: The top bar is 8. The bottom bar shows 54 × 8. Without multiplying, how does 54 × 8 compare with 8?
items.e: 54 is greater than 1 (the top is greater than the bottom), so 54 × 8 is greater than 8. It is more than 1 group of 8. You do not need to multiply. In the picture, the bottom bar has 5 equal parts and the top bar has 4.

items.q: The top bar is 9. The bottom bar shows 23 × 9. Without multiplying, how does 23 × 9 compare with 9?
items.e: 23 is less than 1 (the top is less than the bottom), so 23 × 9 is less than 9. It is only part of 9. You do not need to multiply. In the picture, the bottom bar has 2 equal parts and the top bar has 3.

items.q: The top bar is 6. The bottom bar shows 1 12 × 6. Without multiplying, how does 1 12 × 6 compare with 6?
items.e: 1 12 is greater than 1, so 1 12 × 6 is greater than 6. It is more than 1 group of 6. You do not need to multiply. In the picture, the bottom bar has 3 equal parts and the top bar has 2.

items.q: The top bar is 10. The bottom bar shows 44 × 10. Without multiplying, how does 44 × 10 compare with 10?
items.e: 44 is equal to 1 (the top and the bottom are the same), so 44 × 10 is equal to 10. Multiplying by 1 does not change a number. You do not need to multiply. In the picture, the bottom bar has 4 equal parts and the top bar has 4.
